cards.975: At number nine a cast-iron boot scraper stands in the flags of the front path and its back edge has lifted off the stone along its whole length, leaving a slot closed at both ends and along the top, and means to put one finger in behind it at the near end and draw it gently out against the stone until something stops it, and then to do the same at the far end, and to find out how far it stands off at one end against the other. Nothing lifted, no scraper turned over, no flag taken up, no slot filled, no room entered.
cards.976: At the lock-up a wooden cable drum lies on its cheek in the bay with the last turn of cable lying loose against the inside of one flange, and means to put the fingers in behind that loose turn and walk them right round, following the flange, to find how far the space goes and whether it is the same width all the way. Nothing unwound, no drum rolled, no turn lifted off, no room entered.
cards.977: At the unit a hollow clay block lies on its side on the flags by the office wall with one of its square cells clear, and means to put one finger into that cell and sweep it round the inside, side by side, until all four sides have been felt, and to find out whether the cell is square and how far it goes before it closes. Nothing lifted, no block set upright, no cell filled, no room entered.
cards.978: At number twelve a galvanised bath stands on its side at the shed end of the yard with one rim propped off the flags by a brick, and means to put the hand down under that propped rim until the wrist will not go any further, and to read the depth at the wrist against the outside of the bath, and to find what the rim is standing on. Nothing lifted, no brick taken out, no bath turned over, nothing put in it, no room entered.
cards.979: At number ten a stack of old clay pantiles leans against the shed wall with the row of their rolled heads facing out, and means to put one finger in at the open end of that row and push along from one roll to the next, lifting it a little at each, to find out whether the rolls are all the same and what is behind them. Nothing lifted, no tile drawn out of the stack, no stack knocked over, no line put right, no room entered.
cards.980: At the unit a smoothing plane stands on its side on the bench with its mouth open and the iron still in it, and means to put one finger in through that mouth behind the iron and press it forward along the bed until the iron stops it, and to find out how long the bed is and what lies at the far end of it. Nothing unscrewed, no iron taken out, no shaving cleared, no plane wiped, no room entered.
cards.981: At number twelve a fence post at the shed end of the yard has a square hole cut in it where the end of a rail once sat, and the hole has been packed with leaf litter and nothing else, and means to lay the hand flat on the top of the post and push the fingers down into that square hole until the knuckles come to lie across the post's face, and to find out how deep the hole is and what is at the bottom of it. Nothing dug, no hole filled, no rail fitted, no post moved, no room entered.
cards.982: At number ten a broken spade blade lies in the grass by the shed with the socket empty and the steel tang standing broken in the bottom of it, and means to put one fingertip into that empty socket and turn it against the broken steel, to find out how deep the socket is and what the break left. Nothing picked up, no tang touched, no handle fitted, no hole dug, no room entered.
cards.983: At number nine a small wooden shelf is fixed to the side wall beside the side path on two cleats, and the near cleat has come away from the brick so that the shelf stands a quarter of an inch off the wall and leaves a slot closed at either end by the two cleats, and dust off the roof has packed that slot full; and means to press the pad of one thumb up into that packing until the pad takes the shape of what is packed there, and to find out how deep the packing lies and what is on the brick at the back of it. Nothing unscrewed, no shelf taken down, no cleat refixed, no slot emptied, no room entered.
cards.984: At the lock-up two steel road plates lie one on the other in the bay, the lower one with its edge turned up, and means to press one fingertip down into the shallow hollow that is closed between that turned edge and the face of the plate above, first at the near end and then at the far end, and to find out whether the hollow is the same depth at both. Nothing lifted, no plate turned over, no hollow packed, no room entered.
